body.cap: Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo (left), and Junnyoung Lee, Head of Research at Withforce, take a commemorative photo at the Global Media Meetup held at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Withforce Inc. (CEO Youngmin Kim) announced its participation in the Global Media Meetup on September 1. The event, co-hosted by AVING News and U.S. tech media Ubergizmo, introduced Korean startups’ products and technologies to global markets, with a focus on CES 2026 Innovation Award entries and participants.

Withforce spun out in January 2023 from Hyundai Mobis’ in-house venture program “Startup Challenge.” The company comprises experts with experience in production technology from Hyundai Mobis and global enterprises. Leveraging this expertise, Withforce independently developed a linear muscle actuator (LMA) based on shape memory alloy (SMA).

The company integrates AI technology into its LMA to deliver industrial wearable robots for agriculture, logistics, and construction. These solutions reduce musculoskeletal strain, support worker strength, and enhance workplace safety.

Withforce’s wearable robots feature lightweight structures that deliver up to 25kgf of assistive force, reducing strain on the lower back by up to 35%. Equipped with AI motion mapping and biosignal monitoring, the devices analyze posture in real time, prevent hazardous movements, and send emergency alerts through a control system when needed.

body.cap: Withforce’s agricultural wearable robot Withforce A10 | Image by Withforce

body.x: The company’s flagship product for CES 2026, the Withforce A10, adopts its proprietary LMA as the core actuator. The A10 incorporates more than 200 SMA springs into a compact 3.3kg frame, about half the weight of competitors’ motor-powered devices.

The SMA springs contract and expand when heated, mimicking natural muscle functions. Designed to maximize this effect, the A10 reduces back load during heavy-duty tasks by up to 35%, a result proven through biomechanical testing in industrial sites.
Efficient power consumption allows more than four hours of continuous use without recharging. The device also provides durability and stability suitable for intensive agricultural work.

The AI-driven motion sensing system extends functionality beyond mechanical assistance. It tracks and analyzes user movements in real time, activates support when needed, and prevents harmful motions by predicting excessive muscle strain.

body.cap: Junnyoung Lee, Head of Research at Withforce, during an interview with Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo, at the Global Media Meetup held at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The A10 also integrates biosignal sensors to monitor heart rate variability, muscle load, and fatigue trends. If values exceed thresholds, the system instantly alerts managers or connected devices, enabling timely intervention even for workers in isolated environments.

The product’s ergonomic, breathable design ensures comfort during extended wear. Modular actuators support customization across body types and work environments, while enhancing maintainability and scalability—key factors for mass adoption and global expansion.

“Withforce’s actuator design and robotic control algorithms are protected by patents recognized domestically and internationally,” said Junnyoung Lee. “The A10 can set new standards for wearable robots, improving safety, productivity, and sustainability in agricultural work.”

In 2024, Withforce exported wearable robots to Hyundai Mobis’ EV plant in Georgia, U.S., and is exploring further collaboration with Hyundai Motor Group for continued sales in North America. With CES 2026, the company seeks to secure more international clients. Its A10 robot is expected to resonate in North America, where stricter safety regulations and corporate social responsibility demands are intensifying.

body.cap: Illustration of Withforce A10 in action | Image by Withforce

body.x: Europe is also a key target market. EU initiatives in smart farming and smart manufacturing are driving steady demand for wearable robots, particularly in Germany and France. Withforce aims to secure CE certification and leverage CES 2026 to connect with local distributors of agricultural machinery and industrial safety equipment.

Japan, where an aging workforce accelerates demand for automation in agriculture, is another priority. Withforce plans to compete with established brands like Panasonic and Innophys, while leading overall market expansion.

“Considering international regulations, partnerships with global automakers, and structural demand, Withforce has identified the U.S., Europe, and Japan as its initial export markets,” Lee said. “We will enhance our technology, secure localized certifications, and drive export growth, ultimately becoming a global leader in wearable robotics.”

He added, “By showcasing our philosophy of human-centered design and advanced robotics at CES and other major exhibitions, we will strengthen our global presence. Withforce A10 will open a new chapter for next-generation wearable robots that enhance both worker productivity and safety.”

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo runs Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries, focusing on electronics and technology. It covers major exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen, a former NVIDIA programming engineer and 3D graphics developer, attended the event and has reported annually from CES on global companies’ products and technologies.
